chapter: Willie Lynch, the Blue Rhythm Band and Teddy Hill
title: Blue Rhythm Band trumpets, trombones and Gus Aikin
summary: Looking at a band picture, Holmes works out the trumpets (Wardell Jones, Anderson, Aikin), trombones and banjo, and recalls how he forgot about working with Gus Aikin.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: And Benny James was the banjo player.
I don't know. I worked with Benny in so many different bands. I don't see him here, though. Now, who could that guitar player be?
What about the trumpets?
Well, was that...
Was Wardell Jones there, Preacher Jones, when you came in?
Yeah. Wardell and Anderson.
What about Shelton Hemphill?
Oh, no-no. Not at this time. Gus Aikins is here.
He was apparently there very early.
Holmes (10/11) - 9
But I don't know if he was there when I went in the band or not. Because I worked with Gus in it looked like every band I ever worked in! He was one that got around, too.
Well, according to Rust, the trumpets in the band when you were there, or at least on the recordings...
See, now, you got a band name down here. You've got Gene Aikins, trumpet.
Oh, Gus...
His name is Gus Aikins. Gene was his brother.
Gene Aiken was a trombone player, I think. [DIED 1927]
Yeah. And what name have you got on that...
On the banjo? That's Benny James.
That's Benny James? Oh yeah. Yeah. Now I recognize him. Yeah, I thought that was a trombone he had there. That's a banjo. Harry White.
And Hicks.
Red Hicks.
Red Hicks (Henry) and Harry White were the two trombonists when you were there.
That's right. Two trombonists, three trumpets... Yeah, that's right. Yeah, I guess Gus was in
the band when I went in. That's when I couldn't...
Well, you might have come in at the same time with Hemphill.
No-no-no, I didn't.
You were there before Hemphill.
Man, wait a minute now. It could be at the same time. I don't know. Because I remember Hemphill coming in the band. He was there in the band. But no, I was there a little bit before him.
I see. Well, then, probably Gus Aikin might have been the trumpeter when you were there.
Could be.
But you definitely remember Preacher.
Oh yeah, Preacher I remember.
And Anderson.

Oh, sure. I knew all of them. But I remember... Well, Preacher was such a funny guy anyway. He'd keep you in stitches all the time, you know. Oh, he was funny. Of course, everybody had their own character. Just like Gus. Gus was a showman, too. But I worked with Gus in so many different orchestras. You know? I forgot all about him ever being with the Blue Rhythm. You know, down through the years you get to working over and over and over with the same people with different organizations. You
just forget them sometimes.
